This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The bug report states a NullPointerException occurring in the method isAvailableLocale(Locale). The field cAvailableLocaleSet is a private static Set that is used in isAvailableLocale. The field cAvailableLocaleSet is not initialized in the constructor or statically upfront; rather it is lazily initialized inside the availableLocaleSet() method.

Specifically, availableLocaleSet() checks if cAvailableLocaleSet is null, and if so, initializes it with an unmodifiable set of available locales. Otherwise, it returns the cached set.

However, the failing code path involves a call to isAvailableLocale(Locale), which directly calls cAvailableLocaleSet.contains(locale) without checking if cAvailableLocaleSet has been initialized (i.e., it may be null). This matches the bug report that using cAvailableLocaleSet directly without ensuring initialization causes a NullPointerException.

The failing test method "testLocaleLookupList_LocaleLocale" calls assertLocaleLookupList with various locales, which in turn calls localeLookupList() and likely calls isAvailableLocale() internally (or in related usage). Since cAvailableLocaleSet is not guaranteed to have been initialized before isAvailableLocale is called (as there is no invocation to availableLocaleSet() first), the NullPointerException occurs.

In summary, the root cause is that isAvailableLocale() uses cAvailableLocaleSet directly without lazy initialization checks, causing a NullPointerException if cAvailableLocaleSet has not been initialized yet.

The fix would involve either eagerly initializing cAvailableLocaleSet or ensuring isAvailableLocale() calls availableLocaleSet() to get the initialized set instead of accessing cAvailableLocaleSet directly.

No recent bug reports are relevant to this locale set initialization problem.

This diagnosis fully explains the cause of the NullPointerException as described in the bug report and demonstrated by the failing test.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
